method: Same-agent bilingual close reading of the full language definition and every transition clause, reverse paraphrase of the left-boundary case, and exact structural checks after one documented formula projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: First-order representation of Turing-machine runs, time-indexed predicates, numeric terms, initial configuration, transition axioms and the halting sentence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The language has two-place state/head and tape-symbol predicates. Its first argument represents tape position and its second argument represents execution time. Zero and postfix successor give numerals for both coordinates, while the same less-than predicate orders positions and times.
samples.checks: The separate Q_q and S_sigma families, arities, numeral equations, initial time/position values and all source glossary tokens remain intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For machine M on input w, the language includes predicates for each state and symbol plus 0, successor and less-than. T(M,w) has number-order axioms, the initial state at square one and time zero, the tape-end marker at square zero, input symbols through square k and blanks farther right.
samples.checks: The state-symbol, tape-position/time and k+1-square roles remain exact. Every displayed initial-configuration formula is unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A frame formula preserves tape symbols at squares other than the square overwritten. Right and stay moves write at x and exclude x. A positive-position left move scans and writes x+1 but moves the head to x; its frame must exclude x+1. At square zero a left instruction leaves the head at zero and excludes zero.
samples.checks: The first left-move consequent alone changes A(x,y) to A(x',y), with OLTUR-009 and the exact QA projection. The zero branch remains A(0,y). OLTUR-010 explains that x and y are still free in the frame template, despite the source's sentence label.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: T(M,w) conjoins the listed clauses. E(M,w) says that at some position and time the state-symbol pair has an undefined transition; with a designated halting state it can instead assert that h occurs. The final proposition about numerals m<k is assigned as an exercise with induction on k-m.
samples.checks: Both existential halting formulas, X's undefined-transition definition, the m<k proposition and its three-part reference are source-exact.

source_observations: OLTUR-009: the frozen positive-position left-move clause's A(x,y) excludes the new head position, not the written square x'. The Marathi corrects that one argument and retains the square-zero branch.

OLTUR-010: the displayed frame clauses quantify z but leave x and y free, so they are open formulas until placed within the universally quantified transition axiom. The source calls them sentences; the Marathi adds a bounded clarification.
The following verification unit will need to use the corrected left-move frame argument consistently; its frozen proof has not yet been translated or reviewed.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The corrected transition rule has not yet been tested in a complete built reader.
The next unit's proof is required to establish the proposed reduction.
